transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-22 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marc (Redwood SE), Tara (CSM), Dr. Lena Zhou, Carlos Rivera, Maya Singh, Jon Park (Quantaco)

[00:00] Aisha: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick agenda - go over the numbers from last week's run, look at caching + batching tradeoffs, and confirm next steps. any urgent blockers?
[00:12] Dr. Lena: no blockers, we want to understand the unit economics more - tokens per second per dollar basically, and whether the dedicated or hosted path makes sense.
[00:22] Marc: cool, I'll kick off with the numbers we ran yesterday. so baseline hosted run (no cache, default batching) at your target prompt distribution - average tokens/sec about 450, cost estimate ~ $0.011 per 1k tokens, effective tokens/sec per dollar about 40k tokens/sec per dollar if you annualize, but let me show the slide.
[00:46] Marc: when we enable prefix/KV caching on your common prefixes - which you said is about 28% of requests - we see an effective tokens/sec jump to roughly 800 tokens/sec for the same spend, so that's about 1.7x-1.9x improvement depending on hit rate. importantly that maps to a 22 to 28 percent cost reduction on your passed workloads.
[01:12] Carlos: quick question - when you say tokens/sec per dollar, what's the denominator? is that direct GPU cost or Redwood's hosted rate?
[01:20] Aisha: good call - the spreadsheet uses Redwood hosted per-token rate (list price for pilot bucket), not raw cloud GPU cost; we included a modeled GPU passthrough column as well to show dedicated effective cost.
[01:30] Dr. Lena: and the cache hit assumptions - are those conservatively low? in our logs we think prefix reuse is closer to 35%.
[01:38] Marc: yes we used 28% for the conservative model, if you use 35% the savings push toward 30-33%. I'll attach the paramized sheet.
[01:46] Maya: what's the impact on latency though? we care about tail latencies for our UI flows.
[01:52] Marc: good point - caching tends to help latency for cache hits significantly (sub-10ms for KV proto fetch in our infra), but batching increases per-request latency depending on your batching window. in our tests with batch size target ~16 and a 20ms coalescing window, p95 increased by about 18ms compared to baseline but median stayed similar.
[02:16] Jon: hmm for us p95 matters, 18ms might be ok but if batching is larger to hit better unit cost that could be painful. any middle ground?
[02:24] Marc: yes - you can do adaptive batching and a mixed policy: prioritize low latency for interactive routes (no batching or small window) and enable aggressive batching for background generation. Redwood routing can do per-route policies.
[02:36] Dr. Lena: what's the delta between hosted and dedicated from a unit economics standpoint? we heard dedicated can be 30-40% cheaper at scale but ops overhead is non-trivial.
[02:44] Aisha: our models show dedicated reserved capacity with the quantized model variants brings unit cost down 25-35% depending on commit and utilization. but you need to hit the utilization to realize it - our recommendation for pilots is to prototype caching and batching on hosted first to validate quality and then run a dedicated sizing exercise.
[03:02] Carlos: how deterministic are these numbers? we need ranges for finance.
[03:06] Marc: we've included high/low in the sheet - high assumes 40% cache hit, optimized quantization, and committed utilization; low assumes 20% hit and no quantization. we put an expected case at median.
[03:16] Maya: any security/regulatory concerns with caching? our input can include PII sometimes.
[03:22] Tara: yes - caching is optional and keys can be encrypted and stored per-customer; we also offer per-customer KV isolation in Dedicated or Private. we'll share the security addendum and SOC2 snippets after this call.
[03:36] Dr. Lena: nice. one more - for the longer context (32k) runs how does cost scale?
[03:42] Marc: longer context increases KV traffic and memory pressure, batching behavior also changes. our quick model says unit cost goes up ~1.4x at 32k vs 8k for similar prompt shapes, but caching offset is bigger because more prefix reuse over longer contexts. we'll add 8k/32k columns to the spreadsheet.
[03:58] Carlos: ok great. now on the benchmark you asked us to run - findings?
[04:02] Dr. Lena: we ran the 30-minute test with warmed prefix cache ~20% hit rate, average tokens/sec about 780, median latency 85ms, p95 240ms, cost projection aligned with Marc's numbers.
[04:16] Marc: thanks, that aligns. noted that p95 is a bit high - likely due to occasional KV misses and the way the batching queue was configured.
[04:24] Jon: any log samples we should share for debugging the tail?
[04:27] Carlos: yes we'll upload the run logs to the shared folder after scrub. link: https://redwood.example.com/s/quantaco/poc/logs (note: placeholder link)
[04:36] Aisha: perfect. next, tradeoffs on batching windows - we tested 10ms, 20ms, 50ms. 10ms gave minimal cost savings, 20ms decent, 50ms best unit cost but p95 increases ~60ms.
[04:50] Marc: to quantify: 10ms window -> tokens/sec per dollar baseline+3%, 20ms -> +12%, 50ms -> +28% improvement but p95 hit increases.
[04:58] Dr. Lena: that's useful. for our product we can split interactive calls and bulk inference so maybe a hybrid makes sense.
[05:04] Maya: can Redwood do automatic routing by route?
[05:06] Marc: yes, per-route policies in the console; you can apply low-latency config to certain endpoints and batch-friendly config to others.
[05:12] Aisha: quick recap of next steps - I'll update the cost model and share by Friday, Carlos will run the 1-hour run with warmed cache and share raw logs, Marc will run a sweep of batching windows and push results, and Tara will send security docs. schedule on-prem perf for early May. anything else?
[05:30] Dr. Lena: just one ask - can you include a modeled dedicated sizing with expected qps and cost at 70% utilization? that would help procurement.
[05:38] Aisha: yes we'll add a dedicated sizing tab.
[05:41] Carlos: timeline looks good. we'll try to get logs and run done by Monday/Tuesday next week.
[05:46] Aisha: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the doc and slack channel.
[05:52] (crosstalk) Maya: thanks!
[05:54] Aisha: bye all.
